clue.text: Peel completely, with gusto

blocks.note: zest is the outer peel of a citrus fruit
a plain synonym: wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: Someone stripping the rind off an orange with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'Peel completely' as an instruction to strip a word bare; it is just two synonyms laid side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with gusto means doing it with keen enjoyment and energy, which is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Outsize brassière restrains this exotic creature

indicators.note: restrains means holds in, so the phrase before it keeps the answer captive inside it

blocks.note: read straight through the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A huge bra being used to hold back a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped African wild horse is exotic to a British reader, an animal from a foreign land.

clue.text: Tree used for religious rite

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... tree, a European tree related to the rowan
second meaning: a formal act of worship

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like timber put to a sacred use; the two meanings are unrelated, and the tree is a little-known one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a European fruit tree of the Sorbus genus and a church ceremony of worship.

clue.text: Note the distortion of reality here

definitions.text: Note the distortion of reality here

indicators.note: a distortion twists something out of shape, so the following word is bent into a new letter order

blocks.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader is told to observe how the real world is warped in this story.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a fairy tale is a story that bends reality.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale is a magical story where talking animals and spells replace the facts of ordinary life.

clue.text: It's really surprising if all agree about something at the beginning

indicators.note: at the beginning points to the opening letter of the word just before it
about means turned around and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written
the opening letter only

explanation.surface: It would be astonishing if everyone saw eye to eye on anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said when someone appears unexpectedly in the flesh ('there he was, large as life'), so 'really surprising' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses surprised recognition that someone is really present, in person and unmistakable.

clue.text: Chat a girl up

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Flirting: talking to a woman to win her over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chat ... up' looks like the phrasal verb for flirting, but 'Chat' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to talk at length about trivial things, an informal word for chattering.

clue.text: Wife cut cry short

indicators.note: cut short tells us the word loses its final letter, as a sentence is cut off before its end
short completes the instruction begun by cut: the word stops one letter early

blocks.note: a squawk is a harsh, loud cry, as from a parrot

explanation.surface: A husband silencing his wife mid-complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut ... short' wraps around 'cry': the indicator is split, with 'short' part of the same instruction. The answer is a dated, now offensive term for a Native American woman or wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The old term denoted a Native American woman, especially a married one, so it served historically for a spouse.

clue.text: Kiss and cuddle partner in elopement

blocks.note: first meaning: an old-fashioned verb for courting affectionately
second meaning: in the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle, the dish ran away with this

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a romance; the second half is the cutlery the dish ran off with in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dated verb for lovers canoodling and also names the utensil that eloped with the dish.

clue.text: Single-handed I had parted girl and boy

indicators.note: parted means split open, so something is pushed into the gap between two parts

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
I'd is the contraction of I had
Ed is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A boast of separating a young couple all on one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something single-handed is to manage it without any help from others.

clue.text: Copious supply exhausted, though put to good use

blocks.note: a well is an abundant source, as of water or oil
spent means used up

explanation.surface: A plentiful stock has run out, but at least it went on something worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or time well-spent has been used wisely and profitably, not wasted.

clue.text: Fence with dramatist, right?

blocks.note: J. M. Barrie, the Scottish playwright who wrote Peter Pan
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether fencing with a playwright is the correct thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a verb, as in sword-fighting with the dramatist; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a structure that blocks passage, and a barrier is exactly such an obstruction.

clue.text: Polymath from hill outside Washington

indicators.note: outside says one word sits around the other, enclosing it on both sides

blocks.note: a knoll is a small rounded hill
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: A learned scholar coming down from a hill near the American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little generous: a know-all only thinks they know everything, while a polymath really knows a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with knowledge of everything; the hyphenated noun is the mocking version of the learned person.

clue.text: Just what you need in a little woman — friendliness

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the first phrase goes within the second

blocks.note: 'that's it!' means that is exactly what is wanted
Amy March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A wry remark that what a small woman needs most is a friendly manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little woman' reads as a small lady, but it means a character from the novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is a state of friendly, peaceable relations, so it is a direct synonym for friendliness.

clue.text: English fish on menu perhaps infuriated foreign trio

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it, so the fish goes to the right
perhaps hints that the word is only a possible version of itself, so its letters may be reshuffled

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
these four letters rearranged
the ide is a freshwater fish; plural ides

explanation.surface: An Englishman's fish dish on a menu angering three foreign diners.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'fish on menu' puts the fish after the menu letters. The Eumenides ('kindly ones') is the Greek euphemism for the three Furies, so 'infuriated' is a pun on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides are the three Furies of Greek myth, avenging goddesses: a trio from abroad, full of fury.

clue.text: Wanting to play music, I shove off

indicators.note: off suggests things are out of order or wrong, so the letters are not in their right places

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician eager to perform pushes their way to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks musical, sitting next to 'music', but means playing tricks or pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is eager for playful pranks and naughtiness, keen to make trouble in fun.

clue.text: Soundly pull one's leg — up to a point

definitions.text: one's leg — up to a point

indicators.note: soundly means as heard, so we want a word that is spoken the same as the next one

blocks.note: to tow is to pull along behind

explanation.surface: Teasing someone, but only so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull one's leg' is the idiom for teasing, but the clue splits it: 'pull' is the wordplay, and the leg runs down to its tip, ending at the toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The toe is the far point of the foot, the end where the leg's extension comes to a stop.

clue.text: Announcer has to have the credit for mediating in row

indicators.note: a mediator steps in between two sides, so the phrase goes into the middle of the word that follows

blocks.note: to own is to have or possess
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A spokesman must claim the glory for settling a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as an argument, which the mediating supports; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who walked the streets calling out public notices, an announcer by trade.

clue.text: Beginners find it difficult to evaluate unfinished game

indicators.note: unfinished means the word stops before its last letter is reached

blocks.note: to assess is to judge the value of
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: Novices struggle to judge a half-played game.
explanation.walkthrough: The asses' bridge (pons asinorum) is Euclid's theorem that the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, the classic first hurdle for weak geometry pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to any early test that separates slow learners from quick ones, so novices stumble over it.

clue.text: Resisting having damaged antler cut

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the word's letters are knocked into another order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stag fights back after having its injured antler sawn off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant is unwilling and holds back, offering resistance to doing something.

clue.text: Wife accompanying a student, having the necessary funds

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
herewith means along with this, enclosed alongside
taken as written
L is the learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A wife going along with a student who has enough money.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner comes from the L-plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherewithal means the means or resources needed for a purpose, especially money.

clue.text: Demanding from it information kept concealed ...

indicators.note: something kept concealed is hidden inside, so it sits within the word that holds it

blocks.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex works
taken as written
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Pressing someone for secret information they have hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue, which reuses 'information' for the same slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding a great deal, as of urgent circumstances or exacting people.

clue.text: Fetch twig

blocks.note: first meaning: go and bring something back
second meaning: understand, catch on

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a command to a dog to fetch a stick; 'twig' is the British informal verb for grasping a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both collecting an object and, informally, understanding something, as in 'I don't get it'.

clue.text: ... information it's turned over on a new plant

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the secret is out, now applied to a fresh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentian is a mountain flowering plant famous for its intense blue trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Customers have right to telephone in an empty cafe

indicators.note: empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving only the outside shell of the word
in tells us the first part is placed inside the following shell

blocks.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
TEL is the standard abbreviation for telephone
just the first and last letters kept

explanation.surface: Patrons are entitled to use the phone in a deserted cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is not R here but the legal claim called a lien.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers who use a business, a collective noun for them.

clue.text: Like mast that's unbalanced

blocks.note: first meaning: mast is the fallen nuts of beech, oak and other forest trees
second meaning: informally, mad or crazy

explanation.walkthrough: 'mast' looks like a ship's pole that might be unbalanced; it is the old word for nuts fallen on the forest floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things full of or tasting of nuts, and informally someone mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: In N. America, girth can amount to 100"

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the double-prime mark is the symbol for inches

explanation.surface: Americans can have waistlines of a hundred inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 100" reads as a measurement but is two symbols to spell out: the numeral, then the inch mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a cinch is the strap that holds a saddle on a horse, which the British call a girth.

clue.text: Cast knight out from paradise

indicators.note: out from says something is thrown out of the word that follows, leaving a gap

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A knight banished from paradise, like a fallen angel.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to throw something heavy with effort, as you would cast it away.

clue.text: Sloth is still sloth when reversed

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: inert means motionless
the ai is the three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A paradox: laziness stays laziness however you turn it round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' appears twice with different jobs: first the sin of laziness, then the animal. 'still' is not an adverb but the adjective meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing or remain unchanged, the same idle quality as sloth.

clue.text: What remains after burning tree

blocks.note: first meaning: the powdery residue of a fire
second meaning: a common deciduous tree

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, the remains of a burnt tree; split before 'tree' to get two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the grey residue left by a fire and a familiar hardwood forest tree.

clue.text: Round thing shaped like a keel — it produces music

blocks.note: O is round in shape
carina is the Latin and biological term for a keel or keel-shaped ridge

explanation.surface: A boat-shaped rounded object that makes music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the instrument too: an ocarina is a rounded, egg-shaped wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small vessel flute of clay with finger holes, so it is something that makes musical sounds.

clue.text: Priest prays, preferring others to hear again

indicators.note: preferring others means choosing every other letter, skipping one each time

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A cleric praying, but rather wishing someone else would listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' sounds like other people; here it means the other letters, the even ones. 'hear' is the legal sense, a judge hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a court hears a case when it tries it, so trying a case a second time is hearing it again.

clue.text: It's exciting — each set in doubt

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the following letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Thrilling suspense: every match set hangs in the balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is wavering or uncertainty before acting, the same state of mind as doubt.
